Tracksy privacy policy

Effective 30 October 2026

This policy describes the current Tracksy testing application published by Sourav Sharma DevMatrix. Privacy questions and requests can be sent to souravsharma191919@gmail.com.

Information used by the app

  • Account information: email address, account identifier, display name and preferences, such as currency, language and appearance. Authentication is handled by Supabase Auth. If you choose Google sign-in, Google provides your basic account identifier, email address, name and profile picture to authenticate your account. Tracksy does not request access to your Gmail messages, contacts, Drive files or calendar.
  • Shared financial records: groups and memberships, invitations, expense descriptions, amounts, currencies, categories, dates, split allocations, comments and user-reported settlements. These are records you enter; Tracksy does not access your bank account, read SMS messages or independently verify a transfer.
  • Files you choose: receipts or other supported attachments selected through your device’s file picker, and profile information you provide.
  • Operational information: authentication events and service logs used to operate the backend, prevent misuse and troubleshoot problems. Unsynchronized expense drafts and native login sessions are stored on your device. The Android app also keeps an encrypted, account-scoped cache of profile, groups and overview data to resume faster. Cached overview data expires after seven days and is removed when you sign out.

Why information is used

Information is used to authenticate users, maintain group access, calculate expense shares and balances, preserve a history of corrections and settlements, synchronize records across group members, deliver requested authentication emails, group invitations and user-requested payment reminders, and respond to support or privacy requests.

Who can see shared information

Records and attachments belonging to a group are accessible to authorized members according to their role. Share only information you intend those members to see. A member may download or independently retain information already shared with them. Public receipt access is not provided by the application.

Service providers and storage

The configured backend uses Supabase for authentication, database storage, private file storage and synchronization. The current hosted project is in Sydney, Australia. Google’s Gmail SMTP service delivers authentication emails and group invitations or reminders explicitly requested by group members. Invitation recipients’ email addresses and delivery status are used for that purpose. Reminder emails do not include expense amounts or private financial details. Support requests are received in the publisher’s Gmail inbox. These providers process the information needed to deliver those services. Google Play handles app distribution and may process information under its own policies.

RevenueCat billing, Sentry reporting, Apple OAuth and push delivery are not configured in the current testing build. Receipt OCR and conversational AI are disabled. No advertising SDK is configured, and Tracksy does not sell personal data or provide it for advertising.

Security

The app communicates with the hosted backend over HTTPS. Backend authorization and row-level access policies restrict group records. Receipt storage is private and access links expire. Native session credentials use the device’s secure storage. The hosted web app stores session credentials and selected account data encrypted in browser IndexedDB with an origin-scoped, non-extractable key. These records expire after seven days and are removed on sign-out. Restricted browsers may retain data only for the current tab. Encryption at rest does not prevent access by malicious scripts running on the same origin. The web app caches only its static interface for offline loading; authentication responses and backend records are not placed in the service-worker cache. Security measures reduce risk but cannot guarantee that every device, account or service is free from compromise.

Retention and deletion

Account and group records are retained while needed to provide the service. Expense and settlement histories are shared records and include audit information. Deletion requests are processed manually after account ownership is verified. Support will explain the completion timeline and any data that must remain for other group members, security, dispute handling or applicable legal obligations. Previously downloaded copies held by other users are outside Tracksy’s control. Service-provider logs and backups follow the provider’s retention and recovery processes.

Use Delete account to request account removal and associated personal-data deletion. You may also contact support to request access, correction or deletion of particular information without removing the entire account.

Your choices

You can edit profile preferences, choose which files to upload, sign out and discard local drafts. Corrections or reversals to shared financial records preserve an audit history. Email support if you need help exercising privacy rights available in your region.

Children

Tracksy is not intended for children under 13 and does not knowingly seek their personal information. If you believe a child has provided personal data, contact support so it can be reviewed and removed as appropriate.

Policy changes

This page will be updated when the app’s data practices change. New integrations must be disclosed before their data processing is enabled. The effective date appears at the top of this policy.
